explain.say: A flying bird has four forces on it. Its weight pulls it down and air drag holds it back, so its wings must make lift to hold it up and thrust to push it forward.

explain.say: On the upstroke the bird bends its wing and lets air slip between parted feathers, so it does not push itself back down. Down with power, up with a fold: that rhythm keeps lift and thrust coming.

faq.q: Where does a bird's lift come from?
faq.a: Lift comes from the wing's curved shape and slight upward tilt. The wing turns the air flowing past it downwards, and pushing air down pushes the wing up. Flapping keeps air moving over the wing even when the bird flies slowly.
asks: How do wings hold a bird up?
What is lift for a bird?

faq.q: How does flapping push a bird forward?
faq.a: On the downstroke the outer wing moves down and forward, and its primary feathers twist like propeller blades. They push air backwards, so the air pushes the bird forwards. That push is called thrust.
asks: What makes thrust in bird flight?
Why does flapping move a bird forward?

faq.q: Why don't birds push themselves down on the upstroke?
faq.a: Birds bend the wing at the wrist and elbow on the upstroke, and many part their feathers so air slips between them. The wing meets much less air, so the upstroke costs little and hardly pushes the bird down.
asks: How does a bird lift its wings back up?

faq.q: Why do birds have hollow bones?
faq.a: Many of a bird's bones are hollow, braced inside by thin struts like a bridge, and some connect to air sacs from the lungs. This keeps the skeleton light but strong, so less lift is needed to fly.

faq.q: Which muscles do birds use to fly?
faq.a: Two breast muscles do the work. The big pectoralis pulls the wing down, and a smaller muscle beneath it lifts the wing using a tendon that runs over the shoulder like a rope over a pulley.

facts: In strong flying birds the breast flight muscles make up roughly 15 to 25 percent of body weight.
The muscle that raises a bird's wing sits below the downstroke muscle and pulls through a tendon looped over the shoulder.

quiz.say: Which part of the wingbeat makes most of a bird's lift and thrust?
quiz.show: Which part of the wingbeat makes most of a bird's lift and thrust?
quiz.why: The downstroke drives the spread wing down and forward against the air, making most of the lift and thrust.

wrong.1: On the upstroke the wing is folded or its feathers are parted, so it does little work.
wrong.2: A pause makes no force; between beats a bird can only glide.

quiz.say: Why is a flying bird's breastbone shaped like a deep keel?

options.show: To anchor the big flight muscles

quiz.why: The keel gives the huge breast muscles a large surface to pull from.
